mechanism: Chlorthalidone causes hypokalemia and hyponatremia which may potentiate anticholinergic effects of scopolamine; scopolamine's anticholinergic activity may reduce GI motility and affect chlorthalidone absorption.
action: Monitor electrolytes regularly, assess for excessive anticholinergic effects, and ensure adequate hydration; consider alternative antiemetic if prolonged scopolamine use is needed.
